about: Synthetic, written by a large language model for this project: visitor messages about the recorded walk from the Narikala cable car top station to the Narikala fortress gate in Tbilisi, from visitors with a wheelchair, a stroller, a cane or a walker, older visitors, praise and questions, for evaluation only. No text has been reviewed by a native speaker, and no message comes from a real visitor.

messages.text: The steps right outside the cable car top station were hard for my father, who walks with a cane.
Al salir del teleférico hay escalones enseguida y con la silla de ruedas no pudimos seguir.
요새에서 베틀레미 교회까지 내려가는 긴 계단이 유모차로는 너무 힘들었어요.
The long stairway along the Sololaki ridge has no handrail on some flights, which scared my mum.
Junto a la iglesia de Betlemi hay unos escalones sin pasamanos y mi abuela casi se cae.
Near the bell tower on Askana Street the stone steps have nothing to hold on to.
불의 사원 아테슈가가 정말 인상적이었어요. 꼭 다시 오고 싶어요.
Betlemi Street had several small flights of steps, which made it a slow walk for my grandmother.
Cerca de la catedral armenia hay escalones y con el andador fue muy difícil.
Jemal Ajiashvili Street is all cobblestones and steps, and my partner's wheelchair could not go up.
요새 가는 마지막 계단이 너무 길고 가팔라서 할아버지가 중간에 여러 번 쉬셔야 했어요.
¿La entrada de la fortaleza de Narikala tiene algún acceso sin escalones?
Does the cable car top station have a lift, or only stairs?
The Betlemi church was lovely and the walk there was worth every step.
Los últimos escalones antes de la puerta de la fortaleza son muy altos para una persona mayor.
나리칼라 요새 입구 근처에 화장실이 있나요?
